Rep. Langworthy claims the GOP’s Medicaid plan “strengthens and secures” the program, but the House Budget Committee’s own reconciliation proposal tells a different story. Per-capita caps would slash federal funding by $900B over a decade, forcing states to ration care or kick people off rolls. The claim of “no benefit cuts” collapses when Section 2(b)(9) of the proposal allows states to drop vision, dental, and home-care services under capped budgets.

Work requirements? The 2023 Limit, Save, Grow Act already proved they’d strip coverage from 1.5M Americans—disproportionately hitting rural areas like Western New York. Throwing “EV mandates” into the mix is pure distraction—this bill isn’t about cars, it’s about gutting Medicaid while pretending middle-class taxes are the priority.

Bureaucrats love hiding cuts behind flowery language, but the math doesn’t lie: $2.3T in Medicaid reductions means less care, more suffering, and a broken safety net.
